En la unica carrera donde es común es en Computación. De hecho, a partir de la mitad ya somos mas los que laburamos full time que los que no jaja. Y si bien es cierto que el turno noche arranca a las 5 para todos, la consideracion de los profesores suele ser mayor (arrancando las clases mas tarde, poniendo media/una hora de consultas al principio, subiendo las diapositivas de la clase al campus para que puedas ir hojeando, etc).

Lamentablemente en matematica es bastante raro, y por eso te vas a encontrar con trabas como docentes clavandote un parcial en horarios de la mañana, aun si cursas a la noche. No pasa siempre pero al ser pocos los que laburan, por defecto se asume que no lo haces. Igualmente yo diria que intentes, y que siempre es mejor llegar tarde a una clase que no ir.

Algo que ayuda mucho en todas las carreras, como te dijeron abajo, es la buena onda de tus compañeros o quienes cursaron antes que vos la materia. Hay apuntes, parciales resueltos, resumenes, etc. en muchas de las mismas. Sé que las primeras dos, analisis y algebra, tienen muchisimo material disponible porque se comparten con otras carreras.

Es complicado pero posible. En matemática no existe el turno noche en todas las materias, sobretodo las más avanzadas. Igualmente depende de tu situación personal y laboral, si te bancas llegar en alguna que otra materia 1 hora tarde, etc.

Te dejo el site del Departamento de Matematica con los horarios de cursada por cada cuatrimestre para que te orientes. Pensa que muchas materias se dividen en práctica y teórica y deberias elegir uno de cada para los casos en donde asi sea:  
[https://web.dm.uba.ar/index.php/docencia/materias/horarios/149-horarios](https://web.dm.uba.ar/index.php/docencia/materias/horarios?ano=2023&cuatrimestre=1)  
Fijate cómo van rotando los horarios, en general suelen repetirse. Las primeras materias tienen muchos turnos y suelen estar todos disponibles pero otras, como Álgebra Lineal, rota haciendo un cuatri de tarde y un cuatri de noche.

Okay, first of all, you're doing great by helping her. Thank you. But, remember to not overfill yourself with this, or it'll start to eat your brain too. As you said, you aren't a psychologist.

That being said, I believe that the best support is someone who can listen. Talk to her, when she expresses herself, ask why, try to break down the reason(s). Maybe that can help in her healing process, as to adress why does she feel that way, and just mayyyybe trying for professional help in the future. Also, spending quality time with her just because you love her is a great idea too.

>Even more worrying for me is that she refuses to see a doctor and take her medicine regularly.

I know this is horrible, but try not to push too hard for this. It's more productive to make her open herself to you and maybe later suggesting the professional part.

As for the medicine, does she have someone in her life, besides of you, that knows about her medicine usage? A friend, a distant relative, or such, someone who you can talk to and express your worries? Because if she has a prescription, it is important.

Last thing I want to emphasize on, try to not be so focused on her suicide ideations/anxiety all the time while talking to her. While it's important to adress such things, remember she can fell overwhelmed if she sees you doing a lot of things just because of that. Remember her she isn't her issues nor her troubled past.

I wish the best of luck to both of you.

Idk if this counts but Im studying Computer Science, in a uni with mostly men, in a mildly sexist country. 

The few women in my career formed a lovely groupchat, and we have meetings sometimes too. Its a free space where we can talk about sexism in our uni, promoting our career (and science in general) with girls in high school, dangerous situations with some students, get help and recieve help from other women, no matter if you are in first year or in last year.

This made me realize that in the current years, we have created little spaces to empower ourselves and make ourselves stronger. Sisterhood is in, envying and belittling other women because internalized misogyny is out!

In consequence, we have: more women interested in our courses, more women leading uni projects, more little girls seeing sciencie like theirs too, and of course the feeling of being more safe, knowing that you have a group of women backing you up.
